zenodo.enumerate: GET https://zenodo.org/api/records with q, page, size; use links.next or increment page. Restrict to the specified community and dataset resource_type. Stop at the route max_pages.
zenodo.record: GET https://zenodo.org/api/records/{record_id}; read metadata, access_right, conceptrecid, conceptdoi, files and related_identifiers.
zenodo.download: Use the file entry links.content or links.self, verify open access and file size first. Read complete small artifacts or attempt a bounded byte range. Keep filename and checksum of the original file.
zenodo.license: Read access_right and metadata.license.id (or rights). Record the version DOI, license declaration and any file-level exceptions or terms. Check terms for the intended use before bulk download.
zenodo.deduplication: Use concept DOI/conceptrecid for the asset family, record ID and DOI for a particular version. Compare exact DOI, file checksums, related isIdenticalTo identifiers and original publication pointers across hosts.

huggingface.enumerate: GET https://huggingface.co/api/datasets with author, limit and optional search. Follow the rel=next Link cursor for additional pages up to max_pages.
huggingface.record: GET https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/{repo_id}?blobs=true; retain the SHA, cardData, tags, gated/private state and siblings with sizes and LFS object identifiers. Use the repository tree endpoint if file metadata is incomplete.
huggingface.download: Fetch public files with https://huggingface.co/datasets/{repo_id}/resolve/{sha}/{path}; select small structured samples and license files first. Viewer /splits and /first-rows can expose supported data schema and bounded sample rows.
huggingface.license: Check repository README at the same commit, plus LICENSE or a linked upstream license. Record gating and any third-party notices. A platform label alone does not authorize every use.
huggingface.deduplication: Use lowercased repository ID for family and commit SHA for version; match upstream DOI/repository, LFS SHA-256 and documented repacks. Keep transforms as versions or derivatives unless a genuinely independent data scope is verified.
